description: Tokenization and retrieval word lists for the tool-search tokenizer. UTF-8, LF, one entry per line, no comments.

curation: Lowercase only; one token per line.
Negators (no, not, nor, never) and negative contractions are excluded so query polarity survives.
Content verbs and nouns from the Snowball list (get, make, take, way, well, now, just) are excluded.
Snowball flags will, can, may, might and must as homonym-prone; they are kept because tool-search queries use them as function words.
Positive contractions are kept as single tokens.
Adds closed-class pronouns, determiners, prepositions, conjunctions, auxiliaries and discourse markers only.
Negators and negative contractions remain excluded.
Content nouns and content verbs are excluded; quantity and degree words are kept only where they act as modifiers.

derivedFrom.name: Modern Chinese function-word inventory: particles, pronouns, conjunctions, prepositions, auxiliaries, numerals and classifiers

curation: Negators and negative forms excluded: 不, 没, 没有, 未, 无, 非, 否, 别, 勿, 莫.
Content, existence and modal verbs excluded: 有, 会, 要, 说, 看, 做, 来, 去, 到.
Ambiguous degree and scope adverbs excluded: 只, 仅, 仅仅, 最, 总, 光.
Time units and direction nouns excluded so temporal and positional queries keep their meaning.
Unlicensed third-party Chinese lists (HIT, Baidu, SCU, stopwords-iso) were not copied.

derivedFrom.name: jieba dictionary exposed by @node-rs/jieba/dict
derivedFrom.usage: candidate validation: every entry carries a function POS tag and a dictionary frequency of at least 100

curation: Only words tagged u, y, p, r, c or d in jieba's dictionary were accepted.
Every entry was hand-reviewed; content nouns, time nouns and verb phrases were rejected.
Negators and polarity-bearing forms remain excluded.
No third-party Chinese stopword list was copied.

notes: These files are data only; AgentDefaultCatalog still holds the active retrieval defaults.
English totals 291 entries across core and extended; Chinese totals 325.
The active default list has 65 entries; en-core plus en-extended covers all of them except 'not', which is intentionally retained as a query token.
Chinese tokenization continues to rely on jieba part-of-speech filtering; zh-core and zh-extended are for consumers that need a literal list.
